title: Commonwealth Environmental Protection Act (PL 3-23), 2 CMC 3101-3135
citation: PL 3-23, codified as amended at 1 CMC 2646-2649 and 2 CMC 3101-3135
evidence: Commission Comment in NMIAC chapter 65-10 (https://cnmilaw.gov/docs/admincode/T65/T65-10.pdf, opened 2026-11-10, sha256 e491563c24aa823e74ddeacf4710f7d142f68f665883ada90f5321dc8b9f3f87): "PL 3-23 (effective Oct. 8, 1982), the “Commonwealth Environmental Protection Act,” codified as amended at 1 CMC §§ 2646-2649 and 2 CMC §§ 3101-3135".
notes: Environmental framework Act. 2 CMC 3111 (Policy and Purpose, source PL 3-23 s.2) states the Commonwealth policy of a clean and healthful public environment and sets environmental standards; sections 3111, 3122 and 3131 were read. Implemented in part by the Air Pollution Control Regulations (mp-air-pollution-control-regs, authority 2 CMC 3121 and 3122). title: Recycling Act, 2 CMC 3531-3536 (PL 11-122)
citation: Commonwealth Recycling Act of 1999, PL 11-122, codified at 2 CMC 3531-3536
evidence: Commission Comment under 2 CMC 3531 (https://cnmilaw.gov/docs/cmc_section/T2/3531.pdf, opened 2026-11-10, sha256 77b89922fc95fa887b8f11775ace65a8259329a358092c9722e0ad01a3eda04d): "PL 11-122 that created this chapter took effect February 10, 2000."
notes: Narrower than a carbon price (kept under the keep-and-mark rule, Moka 2026-11-10): Advance disposal fees collected at the point of entry on listed goods (2 CMC 3531 definitions read). A waste fee, not an emissions price; kept as the nearest price-on-pollution instrument. The fee rates in 2 CMC 3532 were not read. title: Air Pollution Control Regulations, NMIAC chapter 65-10
evidence: Chapter History printed in the chapter PDF (opened 2026-11-10, sha256 e491563c24aa823e74ddeacf4710f7d142f68f665883ada90f5321dc8b9f3f87): "Repeal and Reenact Adopted 39 Com. Reg. 40415 (Dec. 28, 2017)". The PDF prints an adoption date, not a commencement date.
notes: Narrower than a greenhouse gas reporting or pricing rule (kept under the keep-and-mark rule, Moka 2026-11-10): Regulations under 2 CMC 3121 and 3122. The permit application sections ask for CO2, CH4 and N2O estimates and apply Prevention of Significant Deterioration to greenhouse gases at 100,000 tpy CO2e; this is a permit-application duty, not a greenhouse gas reporting rule. title: Consumer Protection Act, 4 CMC 5101 et seq. (PL 6-46)
citation: Consumer Protection Act, 4 CMC 5101 et seq., as amended by PL 6-46
evidence: Commission Comment under 4 CMC 5101 (https://cnmilaw.gov/docs/cmc_section/T4/5101.pdf, opened 2026-11-10): "PL 6-46 took effect February 2, 1990." PL 6-46 s.22: "This Act shall take effect upon its approval by the Governor or upon its becoming law without such approval."
notes: Narrower than a green-claims law: 4 CMC 5105 lists unlawful acts, including (e) representing that goods or services have characteristics or benefits they do not have, (g) representing a particular standard, quality or grade, and (m) any act or practice which is unfair or deceptive to the consumer, with no environmental wording. 4 CMC 5112 allows private and class actions. in_force is the date PL 6-46 took effect; the Act replaced portions of the former Consumer Protection Act (33 TTC 351-364).
